copyright: Perseid meteors over Teide Observatory, Tenerife, Spain (© Westend61/Getty Images)
description: Not every summer tradition happens on the ground. Some take place hundreds of miles overhead, one meteor at a time. The Perseids return every year from mid-July through late August, reaching their peak around 12-13 August. Visible across much of the world, they often produce dozens of meteors per hour under dark skies. Picture yourself looking up. One streak appears after another. How many can you spot before you lose count? Each streak comes from debris shed by Comet Swift-Tuttle as Earth moves through its dust trail. The meteors appear to radiate from the constellation Perseus.

copyright: A group of elephants, Amboseli National Park, Kenya (© Ibrahim Suha Derbent/Getty Images)
description: On 12 August, World Elephant Day invites us to pause and consider not just the size of these animals, but the depth of their lives. In places like Amboseli National Park in Kenya—captured in this image—a herd doesn't simply pass through the landscape; it remembers it. Matriarchs guide their families between water sources, tracing routes shaped as much by memory as by terrain.

copyright: Colourful homes line Nyhavn Canal, Copenhagen, Denmark (© emicristea/Getty Images)
description: In Copenhagen, Nyhavn Canal is a burst of colour and history. In Denmark's capital, bright, gabled houses lean towards the water, their reflections rippling beside old wooden ships.

copyright: Joshua Tree National Park, California, United States (© JJ Landscapes/Getty Images)
description: Where two great deserts meet, Joshua Tree National Park reveals a stark, mesmerising landscape shaped by wind, time and extremes. In Southern California, United States, the higher Mojave Desert merges with the hotter, lower Colorado Desert, creating a unique blend of ecosystems and remarkable biodiversity.

copyright: Jean-Marie Tjibaou Cultural Centre, New Caledonia (© Fabien Astre/Alamy)
copyrightKeyword: International Day of the Worlds Indigenous Peoples
description: Today, the International Day of the World's Indigenous Peoples invites a closer look at communities whose stories stretch far beyond recorded history. Proclaimed by the United Nations in 1994 and first observed in 1995, the date marks a landmark 1982 meeting focused on protecting Indigenous rights worldwide. More than 476 million Indigenous people now live across about 90 countries, sustaining thousands of cultures and the majority of the world's roughly 7,000 languages.

copyright: Infinity Bridge in Stockton-on-Tees, England (© Bahadir Yeniceri/Shutterstock)
description: On 8 August, curiosity takes centre stage on International Infinity Day—a celebration inspired by the sideways figure 8, a symbol of something without end. Founded in 1987 by New York–based philosopher Jean-Pierre Ady Fenyo, the date (8/8) was chosen because the number 8, when turned on its side, becomes the infinity symbol, or lemniscate, first introduced by English mathematician John Wallis in 1655. The day celebrates philosophy, science, art and the endless possibilities of human imagination.

copyright: Hot air balloons above Bristol city centre, England (© Rich Jones Photography/Moment/Getty Images)
description: It all started with an idea shared over a pint. Today, that conversation has grown into Europe's largest annual hot air balloon festival. Every summer, the Bristol International Balloon Fiesta fills the skies above Ashton Court Estate with more than 100 colourful balloons, attracting over half a million visitors.
